title: Prime-to-ell tame factors and the continuous fixed summand
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, and a finite intermediate field $E$. For $F=E,\Omega$ use the all-continuous ring $C_F(S)=C(S,F)$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring] and internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Let $r\geq0$, put $L=\mathbf Z_\ell^r$ and $H=(\prod_{q\ne p,\ell}\mathbf Z_q)^r$ with the product topology, where $q$ ranges over primes and $\mathbf Z_q=\varprojlim_n\mathbf Z/q^n\mathbf Z$. Every finite continuous quotient group of $H$ has order prime to $\ell$.

Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space with a jointly continuous $E$-linear $H\times L$-action $\rho$ whose $H$-image $Q$ is finite of order prime to $\ell$. Put $e=|Q|^{-1}\sum_{h\in Q}h$ and $N=M^H=\{v:\rho(h)v=v\text{ for all }h\in H\}$. Then $e$ is a continuous $E$-linear idempotent with image $N$, it commutes with the $L$-action, and $M=N\oplus\ker e$ is a topological direct sum. In a basis adapted to this decomposition, $e$ has matrix $\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$. The subspace $N$ is a finite-dimensional continuous $L$-representation.

For $F=E,\Omega$ set $M_F(S)=C(S,F\otimes_E M)$ and $N_F(S)=C(S,F\otimes_E N)$, using finite-dimensional product norm topologies and the section realizations of [def-sfb-continuous-representation-condensation]. The pointwise extension $e_F$ is a continuous internal idempotent, and the inclusion of $N_F$ identifies it with both $\operatorname{im}e_F$ and the internal $H$-invariants $(M_F)^H$ of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. These identifications preserve the residual $L$-action, are natural in continuous equivariant $E$-linear maps, and commute with $E\to\Omega$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map] via $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. If $r=0$, then $H=L=1$, $e=1$ and $N=M$; zero-dimensional $M$ is allowed.

proof.text: Let $a:H\twoheadrightarrow T$ be a continuous homomorphism to a finite discrete group. Its kernel is an open neighbourhood of zero. By the product topology and the displayed inverse-limit definition of each $\mathbf Z_q$, this neighbourhood contains the simultaneous zero fibre of finitely many residue coordinates $(i,q,n)$. For repeated coordinates with the same $(i,q)$ retain the largest exponent. Thus there is a homomorphism $b:H\to B=\prod_{(i,q)\in J}\mathbf Z/q^{n_{i,q}}\mathbf Z$, with $J$ finite, such that $\ker b\subseteq\ker a$. On $A=b(H)\subseteq B$, define $c(b(h))=a(h)$. The kernel inclusion makes $c$ well-defined, and $c:A\twoheadrightarrow T$ is surjective. This is a direct use of the neighbourhood basis of the specified inverse-limit/product topology; surjectivity of $b$ onto $B$ is not needed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), extracted tame-boundary fixed-summand preparation; finite-cylinder reduction of the finite-quotient assertion

proof.text: Choose one representative in each coset of $A$ in $B$ and in each fibre of $c:A\to T$. Translation gives bijections $B\cong(B/A)\times A$ and $A\cong T\times\ker c$. Consequently $|B|=[B:A]|\ker c||T|$, so $|T|$ divides $|B|=\prod_{(i,q)\in J}q^{n_{i,q}}$. Every $q$ in this product differs from $\ell$. A prime dividing a finite product divides a factor, and $\ell\nmid q^{n_{i,q}}$; hence $\ell\nmid |T|$. This proves the first assertion, including the empty-coordinate product $B=1$. The coset counts are justified by the displayed translation bijections, rather than an uncited group-order theorem.

source.place: Paragraph (3), extracted tame-boundary fixed-summand preparation; explicit finite-set counting after the cylinder reduction

proof.text: The finite $H$-image $Q$ carries a continuous quotient map from $H$. Indeed, choose a finite basis of $M$; the matrix entries of $\rho(h)$ are continuous functions of $h$, by evaluating the jointly continuous action at each basis vector and then applying the $E$-linear coordinate maps. These coordinate maps are continuous by [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-linear-map-continuous], applied over the finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ to the finite-dimensional Hausdorff norm-topological space $M$. Conversely, reconstruction from coordinates is a finite sum of scalar multiples of basis vectors, hence continuous by the topological vector-space operations. Thus any such basis identifies the given topology on $M$ with the product topology on its coordinates; this also applies to the adapted basis constructed in step 5. For a matrix $A$ in the finite image and each different matrix $B$, choose an entry where they differ and an open neighbourhood of that entry of $A$ excluding the corresponding entry of $B$. The finite intersection of the inverse images of these neighbourhoods is open and meets $Q$ exactly in $A$. Thus the finite matrix image has the discrete subspace topology; this also covers rank zero, when the image is a singleton. This proves continuity to the discrete $Q$. The action descends algebraically to $Q\times L$, because $H$ and $L$ commute and the kernel of $H\to Q$ acts trivially. It is jointly continuous: for fixed $q$ choose a lift $h_q$; on the open slice $\{q\}\times L\times M$ its action is $(l,v)\mapsto\rho(h_q,l)v$, a restriction of the given action. Finally $M^Q=M^H=N$, since $H\to Q$ is onto.

source.place: Paragraph (3), extracted tame-boundary fixed-summand preparation; descent of the given action to its finite matrix image

proof.text: The groups $(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)^r$, indexed by positive integers with reduction transitions, have compatible-family limit $L$ with its specified product topology. By [lem-dl-a1-finite-group-limit-profinite], $L$ is compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected; kernels of finitely many residue coordinates give an open-normal identity neighbourhood basis. Thus $L$ is a profinite group, as required below. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-averaging-condensed-invariant-summand] to $W=M$ with this $Q\times L$-action. Its hypotheses hold: $Q$ is finite discrete, its order is prime to $\ell$ by assumption (also by steps 1–3), and the coefficient fields, norm topologies and continuous action are exactly those in its statement. It gives the continuous $L$-equivariant projection $e=|Q|^{-1}\sum_q\rho(q)$ with image $N=M^Q$ and identity restriction to $N$. Therefore $e^2=e$ and $e$ commutes with $L$. It also supplies, for both $F=E,\Omega$, the homeomorphism $F\otimes_E N\xrightarrow{\sim}(F\otimes_E M)^Q$ induced by the invariant inclusion, and its internal realization $N_F\xrightarrow{\sim}(M_F)^Q$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), extracted tame-boundary fixed-summand preparation; finite averaging applied to the descended action

proof.text: Put $K=\ker e$. The maps $N\times K\to M$, $(n,k)\mapsto n+k$, and $M\to N\times K$, $v\mapsto(ev,(1-e)v)$, are inverse continuous linear maps: $e^2=e$ gives the stated codomains and both inverse identities, and continuity into the subspaces follows from the subspace topology. This proves the topological direct sum. From a finite spanning list $(v_j)$ of $M$ [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace], the lists $(ev_j)$ and $((1-e)v_j)$ span $N$ and $K$. In each list delete a vector whenever it lies in the span of its predecessors; span is unchanged and the final lists are independent, hence bases. Their concatenation is a basis of $M$ by the direct-sum identities, and the matrix of $e$ in it is $\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$. The $L$-action preserves $N$ because it commutes with $e$; its restriction $L\times N\to N$ is continuous by the subspace topology. Thus $N$ is a finite-dimensional continuous $L$-representation.

source.place: Paragraph (3), extracted tame-boundary fixed-summand preparation; explicit splitting, adapted basis and residual representation

proof.text: First, the tensor-extended $H\times L$-action on $F\otimes_E M$ is jointly continuous for either $F$: by the argument of step 3, applied to $(h,l)\mapsto\rho(h,l)v_j$ and the $E$-linear coordinate maps, continuous by [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-linear-map-continuous], the matrix entries $a_{ij}(h,l)\in E\subseteq F$ of $\rho(h,l)$ in the basis $(v_j)$ are continuous. In the product topology of the basis $(v_j\otimes1)$ the action is $((h,l),\sum_jc_jv_j\otimes1)\mapsto\sum_{i,j}a_{ij}(h,l)c_j\,v_i\otimes1$, a finite sum of products of continuous functions in the topological field $F$. The same holds for $N$ with its restricted $L$-action. Hence [def-sfb-continuous-representation-condensation] supplies the section realizations $M_F$ and $N_F$ used below. Extend the adapted basis to $F$ using [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension]. The tensor extension of $e$ has the same matrix $\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$ in the finite-dimensional product norm topology, so is continuous for either $F$, and is still idempotent. By [def-sfb-continuous-representation-condensation], postcomposition defines its internal $C_F$-linear endomorphism $e_F$ on $M_F$. The invariant inclusion and the projection onto its first coordinates give inverse sectionwise identifications of $N_F$ with the image of $e_F$: a section fixed by $e_F$ has zero complementary coordinates, and its remaining coordinates are continuous. The construction commutes with restriction along every continuous map of test spaces, so these are internal module maps. The $L$-equivariance follows from $e\rho(l)=\rho(l)e$ and the same tensor identity.

source.place: Paragraph (3), extracted tame-boundary fixed-summand preparation; tensor matrix and sectionwise image of the continuous internal projector

proof.text: Use the definition of internal invariants in [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. For a profinite $S$, a section $x:S\to F\otimes_E M$ which is internally $H$-fixed has $x(s)$ fixed by every $h\in H$: pull back along $s:*\to S$ and use the constant generalized element $h$ on $*$. Conversely, if every $x(s)$ is $H$-fixed, then for every $u:T\to S$ and $g:T\to H$ the equality $\rho_F(g(t))x(u(t))=x(u(t))$ holds for every $t$, so $g\cdot u^*x=u^*x$ as continuous maps. Pointwise $H$-fixed equals pointwise $Q$-fixed by surjectivity. The homeomorphism in step 4 therefore identifies this space of sections precisely with $C(S,F\otimes_E N)=N_F(S)$; continuity into the invariant subspace is measured with its subspace topology. These identifications are the actual invariant inclusions, commute with restrictions, and retain the residual $L$-action. Together with step 6 this identifies $N_F$ with both internal objects claimed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), extracted tame-boundary fixed-summand preparation; generalized-element test for H-invariants and identification of the two images

proof.text: For an $H\times L$-equivariant continuous $E$-linear map $f:M\to M'$, the finite $H$-images need not coincide. Use the common image $R$ of $H\to Q_M\times Q_{M'}$. Both component quotient maps are continuous by step 3, so their product is continuous; the same map with codomain its image $R$ is continuous by the subspace topology. The finite product and its subspace $R$ are discrete. Steps 1–2 give $|R|$ prime to $\ell$. Each projection $R\twoheadrightarrow Q_M$ or $Q_{M'}$ has fibres given by translates of its kernel. Hence the average over $R$ acting on either representation is its original average: each summand is repeated $|\ker(R\to Q)|$ times and $|R|=|\ker(R\to Q)||Q|$. Now $f$ intertwines each $R$-operator, so summing gives $e'f=fe$. Alternatively the naturality clause of [lem-sfb-finite-averaging-condensed-invariant-summand] applies to this common $R$. Restriction of $f$ to invariants and tensoring therefore commute with all inclusions and retractions; postcomposition realizes these same equalities internally [def-sfb-continuous-representation-condensation]. This proves naturality even when the finite image changes.

source.place: Paragraph (3), extracted tame-boundary fixed-summand preparation; common finite image for naturality in arbitrary equivariant maps

proof.text: For the continuous coefficient inclusion $E\to\Omega$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map], the finite-sum formula gives $e_\Omega(1\otimes v)=1\otimes e_E(v)$, as also asserted by [lem-sfb-finite-averaging-condensed-invariant-summand]. Tensor insertion commutes with the invariant inclusion, with $1-e$, and with the restricted equivariant maps. Applying these identities pointwise proves the coefficient squares for both the image and invariant identifications; all preserve $L$. If $r=0$, the empty products $H,L$ are trivial, $Q=1$, the average is the identity and $N=M$; each inclusion and projection is then the identity under the canonical tensor-unit identification. If $M=0$ or $N=0$, the corresponding basis and section coordinates are empty and the same formulas apply. On the empty profinite test set every continuous-function module has its unique zero section. No completeness of $\Omega$ is used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), extracted tame-boundary fixed-summand preparation; coefficient identity and degenerate cases
